evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: shape; Shuowen; historical meanings; phonetic component
evidence.text: The entry displays a seal form, one bronze example, and four manuscript examples, with no oracle-bone example in the entry. It analyzes the bronze form as 水 plus phonetic 曷 and reports 渴 used for 竭 in “water dried up/exhausted” contexts, including the Zhongshan King Fanghu and a Mawangdui Laozi manuscript. It quotes the Shuowen gloss 盡也 and 从水、曷聲. It separately cites the Shijing line 苟無飢渴 for thirst, a Tang Bai Juyi example for dry/parched, and a Gongyang zhuan use meaning urgent. These are the database’s analyses and citations; they do not establish all intermediate semantic stages or the earliest surviving physical witness of the Shijing line.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 渴

evidence.source: Palace Museum-hosted PDF, 中山王方壺 inscription transcription
evidence.text: The text includes 貫渴（竭）志盡忠 and dates the vessel to the Zhongshan king’s fourteenth year. This transcription supports the reading as 竭 but does not independently show the exact inscribed graph; CUHK supplies the claim that the graph was 渴.
evidence.kind: primary inscription transcription in museum-hosted source
evidence.title: 中山王譬壺 (PDF transcription)

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry quotes 曷 as 何也，从曰、匃聲, with fanqie 胡葛切; its Middle Chinese classification is 匣母, entering tone, 山攝寒/曷開一. Its bronze-form discussion says the middle element is unclear, so the depicted original referent is not secure. That uncertainty does not by itself negate 曷’s phonetic role in 渴.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 曷

evidence.text: The entry analyzes 氵 as the meaning component and 曷 as the sound component, calls 氵 a component form of 水, and labels the displayed 渴 forms bronze script (Late Warring States, about 250 BCE), Shuowen seal script (about 100 CE), and Eastern Han clerical script. Its readings table gives 渴 *Nə-[k]ʰˤat (Old Chinese, Baxter–Sagart notation) and 曷 *[g]ˤat (Old Chinese, Baxter–Sagart notation). The site's two historic glyph image URLs could not be opened, so the glyphs and labels were not visually checked here.
evidence.kind: character dictionary; secondary component and chronology account
evidence.title: 渴 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.field: 曷 component history and phonetic series
evidence.text: The entry lists 曷 as a sound component in 渴 and other characters and gives Old Chinese *[g]ˤat, Middle Chinese hat, hé. It proposes a specific original depicted fruit and says the modern interrogative sense is a phonetic loan, but this is a secondary account and the inspected sources do not establish that depicted referent independently. Shuowen instead analyzes 曷 as 从曰、匃聲. This proposed origin for 曷 is not necessary to support its later sound-component role in 渴.
evidence.kind: secondary character dictionary; competing graphic-origin proposal
evidence.title: 曷 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart local dataset rows supplied in local_primary_readings
evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 1886 for 渴 and row 1245 for 曷; exact rows supplied by harness
evidence.text: Exact supplied rows: 渴 py kě, MC khat, OC *Nə-[k]ʰˤat, gloss thirsty; 曷 py hé, MC hat, OC *[g]ˤat, gloss what. These preserve the local dataset’s notation and show matching final/coda material but distinct initials in this reconstruction. I did not independently inspect the filesystem in this research turn; the rows were provided in the input. The official character-specific Unihan lookup URLs were attempted but inaccessible, so no verified upstream character page supports citing these local rows externally.
evidence.kind: local dataset reading cross-check; exact rows provided in input
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup (per-character pages attempted; inaccessible)

evidence.source: Wiktionary file description, mirrored Commons metadata
evidence.field: 渴-seal.svg identity, source lead, license, file history
evidence.text: The description identifies the SVG as 渴 in Shuowen seal-script style, names S08263 on hanziyuan.net as the character-specific image lead, and states public-domain licensing for the SVG. It records the file history as created 14 December 2014 by Micheletb. The Commons page and image URL could not be opened directly; the file-description content was available through Wiktionary’s mirrored Commons metadata, but the image pixels themselves were not accessible for visual verification. The image should therefore not be represented here as visually inspected.
evidence.kind: file-description mirror; image identity not visually verified
evidence.title: File:渴-seal.svg - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The entry labels 渴 a phono-semantic character formed from 水 and 曷, shows a Warring States bronze form and a Han Shuowen small-seal form, and lists 渇 as the Japanese shinjitai counterpart. Its graphics support the broad component analysis but are secondary and do not independently date the earliest physical witness or establish the semantic bridge from dried up to thirsty.
evidence.title: 渴 - ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.text: Attempted the exact official character lookup URLs for 渴 (U+6E34) and 曷 (U+66F7), but the web tool could not access either. The local supplied rows report kě and hé respectively, but current readings could not be confirmed from the official character-specific pages in this turn. Unicode search results confirmed the Unihan lookup service exists, not those exact values.

search_audit.outcome: Search found the CUHK entry and competing/parallel character-dictionary descriptions. The CUHK page was opened and inspected; it supports the bronze component analysis and distinct senses. Commons’ exact 渴-seal page did not open on a direct URL; a later search exposed the mirrored Wiktionary file description.

search_audit.outcome: Both exact Unicode Unihan lookups were attempted but inaccessible. The Palace Museum-hosted transcription search result included the Fanghu phrase and date context; its transcription prints 渴（竭） rather than reproducing the graph image.

Search retrieved the file-description metadata mirrored from Commons: seal-script label, S08263 character-image lead, public-domain claim, and 2014 file history. Opening the description and original asset through the web tool failed; pixels were not inspected.

search_audit.query: 曷 何也 从曰 匃声 读音; Unicode Unihan exact kMandarin 渴 and 曷
search_audit.outcome: CUHK search returned the character-specific 曷 dictionary page content: Shuowen analysis, fanqie, Middle Chinese classification, and uncertain bronze interior. Official Unicode endpoints remained inaccessible.

gaps: The candidate seal SVG metadata reports the right character and style, cites S08263, and gives public-domain status, but neither the Commons page nor direct asset was opened; pixels, attribution chain, and direct image provenance remain unverified. Do not claim visual inspection or rely on metadata alone for an image selection.
The CUHK report of no oracle-bone example applies to its displayed entry only, not all corpora. No complete dated glyph sequence was established.

CUHK reports the Zhongshan King bronze reading as 渴 used for 竭, but the opened inscription transcription prints 竭 and cannot independently confirm the exact graph. The Fanghu is dated to the king’s fourteenth year (about 314 BCE in the cited dossier), while the Mawangdui example is Han; exact graph witnesses require paleographic verification.
CUHK cites a Shijing thirst use, but the earliest surviving physical witness of that line was not established. The chronology of texts cited is not a chronology of the character’s senses.

The movement from ‘exhausted/dried up’ to ‘thirsty/parched’ is plausible but lacks dated bridging attestations. The separate ‘urgent’ use is recorded, but its semantic connection to the other senses is unestablished.

The Dong Chinese proposal that 曷 originally depicted cut fruit is not independently verified; the ancient 曷 referent remains uncertain in the CUHK account. This does not negate 曷’s documented sound-component analysis in 渴.

Local exact Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were supplied in the input, but this turn could not independently inspect the repository files. The official per-character Unihan pages were attempted and inaccessible; secondary sources were not substituted as proof of the current Unihan kMandarin values.

The formation analysis 氵/水 plus 曷 is supported. The precise graphic transition from bronze 水 to modern left-side 氵 is not traced in the inspected sources. No local extract is recommended because reuse terms for the repeated CUHK research material were not verified and the candidate image remains visually unverified.
